title: Add and subtract mentally with friendly numbers, compensating and decomposing

lesson.title: Friendly Numbers: Add the Easy Way, Then Fix It

steps.say: You already know that adding two hundred to a number is easy — you just bump the hundreds. But what if you have to add one hundred ninety-nine? That number looks messy, and today we will learn a little trick that makes it just as easy.

Here is the whole idea. Look at one hundred ninety-nine on the number line. It is sitting right beside two hundred — only one step away. So instead of adding the messy number, we add the friendly number two hundred, and then we take one step back, because we added one too many.

visual.caption: One hundred ninety-nine is only one step from friendly two hundred.

steps.say: Let us try it with real money. Your school raised three thousand four hundred eighty-six dollars for the food bank, and then a neighbour donates one hundred ninety-nine dollars more. First, make the friendly jump: three thousand four hundred eighty-six plus two hundred is three thousand six hundred eighty-six. That one is easy to do in your head.

visual.caption: One big friendly jump of two hundred.

steps.say: But wait — the neighbour gave one hundred ninety-nine dollars, not two hundred. We pretended they gave one extra dollar, so now we hop one step back. Three thousand six hundred eighty-six minus one is three thousand six hundred eighty-five. So the school has three thousand six hundred eighty-five dollars.

visual.caption: One tiny hop back, because we added one dollar too many.

steps.say: Here is the mistake I see most often. Some kids jump forward two hundred and then jump forward one more, and get three thousand six hundred eighty-seven. Think about it with the dollars: we already counted one dollar that was never given, so we must take it away, not add another one. If you added too much, you give some back.

visual.caption: Wrong way: hopping forward again makes the total too big.

steps.say: So remember: make it friendly, then fix it. Round up to the nice number, jump, and step back the little bit you borrowed.

lesson.answer: Add the friendly number first, then give back the extra you borrowed.

practice.question: Maya's family is saving for a camping trip to Tofino. They have four thousand two hundred seventy-five dollars saved, and this month they add two hundred ninety-eight dollars more. Use a friendly number to add it in your head — what friendly number would you use, and how much do they have now?
practice.answer: Use three hundred. Four thousand two hundred seventy-five plus three hundred is four thousand five hundred seventy-five, then step back two dollars because you added two too many. They have four thousand five hundred seventy-three dollars.
